A successful end to another important Starship flight test.

BREAKING: Starship has deployed Starlink V3 satellites for the first time. 

• Marks the first-ever deployment of Starlink V3 satellites from Starship.
• A major milestone for SpaceX's next-generation satellite network.
• Demonstrates Starship's capability to carry and deploy larger, more advanced payloads than Falcon 9.

A key step toward scaling Starlink with the world's most powerful launch system.

NEWS: SpaceX shares the latest update ahead of Starship Flight Test 13. 

• Clear skies are allowing teams to closely monitor Starship's heat shield tiles during ascent one of the mission's primary test objectives.
• The previous launch attempt was scrubbed due to poor visibility.
• SpaceX says Starship is certified to launch in lightning conditions, but the capability will be introduced cautiously as launch cadence increases.
• Propellant loading is progressing normally, including the ship's header tanks, which will be used for the in-space relight and landing burn.
• Liftoff is currently targeted for 5:51 p.m. CT, a few minutes into today's launch window.

Weather and fueling remain on track as SpaceX prepares for another Starship test flight.

Video

NEWS: SpaceX reveals how it prepares Starship for flight. 

• SpaceX prioritizes rapid testing to avoid "analysis paralysis" and accelerate development.
• A recent static fire was aborted after vibration triggered pad sensors protecting the flame diverter.
• Engineers adjusted the system to prevent false aborts while maintaining safety.
• Pad 2's flame diverter uses around 650,000 gallons of water per minute roughly the volume of an Olympic-sized swimming pool every minute to absorb the immense heat from launch.
• At liftoff, Starship's 33 Raptor engines consume about 65,000 pounds of propellant every second, generating nearly 18 million pounds of thrust.

The behind-the-scenes look highlights the engineering challenges of operating the world's most powerful launch system.

THE “FAR RIGHT” LABEL IS A FRAUD

Legacy media keeps calling basic common sense “far right.”

Look at the list they’re attacking:

• Secure borders
• Safe cities
• Sensible spending
• Fair justice system
• Free speech
• Self-protection
None of these are extreme. These were completely normal positions for most of modern history — including under Democrats just 10–15 years ago.
When the media has to redefine the center as “far right” in order to win an argument, they’ve already lost the debate.
Elon put it simply in the Economist interview: he supports normal people, and the media’s framing is false and misleading.
The more they overuse these labels, the less power they have.
